notes:
## Changes

- **Watch on phone.** Browse your collection and play scenes on a phone or tablet in its web browser, on the same Wi-Fi, while Video Shelf is open on your PC. Nothing to install. Switch it on in Settings › Phone and tablet. It's off until you do.
- **Connect with a QR code.** Scan the code in Settings with the phone's camera and your library opens. The phone stays connected for 30 days. A PIN is optional, for devices without a camera.
- **Folders, Latest scenes, Performers, Studios, Tags and search** on the phone, with a player for each scene. The phone can only look: it can't change, move or delete anything.
- **Choose which videos can play:** only files phones can play directly (very little work for the PC), also MKV and similar files (the PC re-wraps them as they play), or everything else as well (the PC converts them as they play, which works it hard). Needs ffmpeg for the last two. Use "Start from" on the phone to skip ahead in those.
- **Downloads tab:** see what's arriving in your downloads folder, newest first, as it happens. Tap a finished download to play it. "Hide unfinished downloads" leaves out files still arriving.
- **Drives tab:** free space on your drives, including where downloads, favourites and safety copies go, with a warning when one is running low.
- Private: only devices on your home network can connect, never the internet. Hidden categories stay hidden, and watching on a phone doesn't count as a play.
linuxNotes:
First Linux preview of Video Shelf: the whole app on Ubuntu and similar systems (.deb). It uses the same catalogue as the Windows app.

Install with:

    sudo apt install ./videoshelf_0.12.0_amd64.deb
